page: Amazon Web Services i8g.4xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual instance built on the AWS Nitro architecture. Powered by 64-bit arm64 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processors running at 2.8 GHz, the configuration supplies 16 dedicated physical cores with one thread per core, avoiding hyperthreading resource contention. The processor integrates 64 KB L1 data cache and 2 MB L2 cache per core alongside 36 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is provisioned at 128.0 GB, yielding a high ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage architecture features a dedicated 3,750 GB local NVMe SSD, delivering high-density non-volatile capacity directly attached to the host. Network interfaces provide a baseline throughput of 9 Gbps, and no discrete GPUs are present.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong performance across the memory subsystem and storage operations. In uncached large-block evaluations, memory read bandwidth reaches 296.95 GB/sec and write bandwidth achieves 130.36 GB/sec, placing memory throughput in the upper quartile, alongside a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3,336.33. Multi-core scaling is demonstrated by a multi-core Geekbench score of 15,908.0 and PassMark database operational metrics of 24,105.77. Parallel throughput extends to data decompression, where multi-threaded bzip3 achieves 202.88 GB/sec. Tradeoffs appear in raw single-core execution and generative AI workloads; lacking dedicated tensor accelerators or AVX instructions, text generation performance on large language models remains constrained.

By bundling significant local NVMe capacity with generous memory per core on energy-efficient Arm architecture, the i8g.4xlarge offers a favorable cost-efficiency profile for I/O-intensive workloads without relying on external network-attached volumes. It is suited for transactional relational databases, high-capacity NoSQL clusters, in-memory data stores like Redis, search indexing, and real-time log ingestion systems.
description: Amazon Web Services i8g.4xlarge is a storage-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, featuring 16 dedicated arm64 AWS Neoverse-V2 cores clocked at 2.8 GHz without hyperthreading. It couples 128.0 GB of memory, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation, with a bundled 3,750 GB local NVMe solid-state drive and 9 Gbps baseline network throughput. The instance includes no GPU acceleration. Benchmarks reflect exceptional memory subsystem performance, achieving top-tier PassMark memory scores and strong uncached read and write bandwidth exceeding 296 GB/sec and 130 GB/sec, respectively. Multi-core performance is robust, with high ratings in database operations and parallel decompression, though LLM token generation remains constrained by the absence of dedicated matrix accelerators. Offering high storage density alongside substantial RAM per core, i8g.4xlarge represents a cost-efficient deployment profile for high-throughput relational and NoSQL databases, in-memory caches, search engines, and real-time analytics pipelines requiring low-latency local NVMe I/O.
